examples.attribution: Li et al. (2019) / CheckMate 025 队列分析
examples.conditions: 人群：接受Nivolumab或Everolimus治疗的晚期肾细胞癌患者；分组依据：基线血浆肌苷水平的中位数分为高/低两组；指标：总生存期（OS）。
examples.finding: 在肾细胞癌（RCC）患者队列（CheckMate 025试验，Nivolumab治疗组 n=394, Everolimus对照组 n=349）中，通过非靶向代谢组学分析发现，只有肌苷水平与免疫检查点阻断（ICB）的总生存期（OS）显著相关。具体而言，基线血浆肌苷水平较高的Nivolumab治疗患者中位OS为33个月，而低肌苷水平患者的中位OS为22个月。这种关联仅在Nivolumab（抗PD-1）治疗组中存在，而在Everolimus（mTOR抑制剂）治疗组中未观察到显著差异。
examples.use_in_review: 提供人类实体瘤患者血浆中肌苷浓度与ICI疗效的相关性数据，特别是生存期差异。

examples.attribution: 本研究 (Inhibition of UBA6 by inosine...)
examples.conditions: 动物模型：B16-F0黑色素瘤小鼠，ICI治疗前后对比；临床队列：22名接受Sintilimab（抗PD-1）治疗的实体瘤患者，基于肿瘤组织UBA6蛋白表达（IHC评分）分组；指标：肿瘤体积、生存率、总体响应率（ORR）、UBA6蛋白表达水平。
examples.finding: 在小鼠模型中，携带B16-F0肿瘤的野生型小鼠血浆肌苷水平高于无肿瘤小鼠，但在接受ICI（抗PD-1 + 抗CTLA-4）治疗后，血浆肌苷水平下降。在人类临床验证部分，研究纳入了22名接受抗PD-1治疗的不同实体瘤（食管癌、肺癌、胃癌、结肠癌等）患者，发现部分缓解（PR）或疾病稳定（SD）患者的肿瘤组织中UBA6蛋白表达水平显著低于疾病进展（PD）患者。低UBA6表达组的总体响应率（ORR）为50%，高UBA6表达组为17%。虽然本研究未直接报告这22例患者血浆肌苷的具体浓度范围，但证实了UBA6低表达（模拟肌苷抑制效果）与良好ICI疗效正相关。
examples.use_in_review: 补充说明肌苷在动物模型中的变化趋势及临床样本中UBA6表达与疗效的关系，作为肌苷-UBA6轴的临床相关性佐证。

question_material.explanation: 该研究通过代谢组学筛选和临床队列分析，确立了血浆肌苷水平与免疫检查点阻断（ICI）疗效的正相关性。机制上，肌苷并非仅作为能量来源或作用于免疫细胞，而是直接进入肿瘤细胞，抑制泛素激活酶UBA6的活性。UBA6的抑制导致肿瘤细胞内FAT10依赖的抗原加工和炎症信号通路改变，上调MHC-I类分子表达和干扰素反应基因，从而增强肿瘤内在免疫原性，使其对T细胞介导的细胞毒性更敏感。在临床上，肿瘤细胞中UBA6的高表达预测了较差的ICI疗效，而低UBA6表达则与更好的生存期和响应率相关，提示肌苷或其类似物可能通过靶向UBA6来克服ICI耐药。
remaining_points: 原文指出由于腺苷在体内半衰期极短（约10秒），而肌苷较长（约15小时），且样本缺失，本研究未在临床队列中直接测量血浆肌苷浓度，因此缺乏人类实体瘤患者血浆肌苷的具体浓度数值范围数据。
临床验证队列样本量较小（n=22），限制了统计效力。

broader_review_uses.connection_to_review: 背景与概念框架
broader_review_uses.material: 论文指出肿瘤代谢环境改变（如营养短缺、腺苷积累）导致免疫抑制性TME，而肌苷作为腺苷代谢物，其水平受肠道微生物群失调影响。
broader_review_uses.purpose: 用于综述中构建‘代谢-免疫’交互作用的背景，说明代谢物不仅是能量底物，也是调节免疫微环境的关键信号分子。

broader_review_uses.connection_to_review: 实例与反例
broader_review_uses.material: 肌苷在B16和4T1模型中有效，但在低UBA6表达的MC38模型中无效；肌苷不直接作用于T细胞，而是作用于肿瘤细胞。
broader_review_uses.purpose: 用于综述中强调机制的情境依赖性（context-dependency），即同一代谢物在不同肿瘤类型或不同分子背景下可能产生不同效果，避免过度概括单一机制。

broader_review_uses.connection_to_review: 实践知识与转化潜力
broader_review_uses.material: 肌苷作为膳食补充剂已长期使用，安全性良好；UBA6表达可作为预测ICB疗效的生物标志物。
broader_review_uses.purpose: 用于综述中讨论现有药物的老药新用（repurposing）潜力，以及生物标志物指导下的精准免疫治疗策略。

facet_contributions.boundaries: 主要基于小鼠模型和有限的临床队列；肌苷的来源不仅限于肠道微生物（也可由癌细胞分泌），需结合其他文献明确其在不同情境下的主要来源。
facet_contributions.contribution: 提供了肌苷（一种由肠道微生物群产生或受其影响的代谢物）与ICB疗效正相关的临床和体内证据。展示了肌苷水平可作为预测ICB响应的生物标志物。
facet_contributions.possible_uses: 用于综述中讨论肠道微生物群代谢产物如何作为系统性信号调节抗肿瘤免疫，特别是那些能够进入血液循环并作用于远端器官（如肿瘤）的代谢物。

facet_contributions.boundaries: 机制主要在黑色素瘤和乳腺癌模型中验证；UBA6在其他类型实体瘤中的作用可能不同（如MC38结肠癌模型中UBA6低表达导致肌苷无效）。
facet_contributions.contribution: 揭示了肌苷增强ICB疗效的具体分子机制：直接结合并抑制肿瘤细胞内的UBA6（泛素激活酶），从而解除其对炎症信号和抗原呈递通路的抑制，增强肿瘤细胞对T细胞介导杀伤的敏感性。
facet_contributions.possible_uses: 用于综述中阐述代谢物调节肿瘤细胞内在状态的机制案例，特别是通过调控泛素化系统或表观遗传/转录后修饰来改变肿瘤免疫原性的路径。

facet_contributions.boundaries: UBA6作为靶点的普适性需在不同肿瘤类型中进一步验证；目前证据显示其效果依赖于肿瘤细胞的基础UBA6表达水平。
facet_contributions.contribution: 证明了UBA6是肿瘤内在的免疫检查点，其高表达导致免疫抑制性微环境和ICB耐药，而UBA6缺失或抑制可逆转这一过程。
facet_contributions.possible_uses: 用于综述中讨论肿瘤内在因素（如特定酶的表达）如何决定肿瘤对免疫治疗的敏感性，以及这些内在因子作为治疗靶点的潜力。

review_planning_B.planning_summary: 该论文提供了关于肠道微生物群衍生代谢物（肌苷）如何通过直接靶向肿瘤细胞内在机制（UBA6抑制）来增强免疫检查点抑制剂（ICB）疗效的具体证据。它填补了“微生物代谢物-肿瘤细胞内在属性-免疫响应”这一链条中的关键分子机制空白，特别强调了肿瘤细胞并非被动受体，而是通过代谢感应主动调节其免疫原性。这对于解释为何某些微生物组成有利于ICB响应，以及如何通过代谢干预克服肿瘤内在耐药性具有重要参考价值。
scope_interpretation_cautions: 肌苷的来源具有多源性（肠道微生物、饮食、癌细胞自身），本论文侧重于其作为循环代谢物对肿瘤细胞的直接作用，解读时需区分其与肠道微生物群的间接联系与直接靶向关系。
UBA6的作用具有肿瘤类型特异性，不能将其在所有实体瘤中的功能外推至所有情况，需注意不同肿瘤细胞系中UBA6基础表达水平的差异对治疗效果的决定性影响。
临床数据的局限性：人类队列中未直接测量肌苷水平（因技术困难），主要依赖UBA6表达作为下游效应指标，解读临床相关性时需保留这一推断性质。

study_summary_A.approach: 1. 代谢组学筛选：对接受抗PD-1/抗CTLA-4联合治疗的B16-F0荷瘤小鼠血浆进行非靶向代谢组学分析；重分析人肾细胞癌（RCC）患者CheckMate 025临床试验的血浆代谢数据。 2. 体内药效学评估：在B16-F0（敏感）、B16-GMCSF（抵抗）和4T1（抵抗）小鼠模型中，评估单独使用肌苷、ICB或两者联合治疗的肿瘤生长和生存率。 3. 单细胞转录组与流式细胞术：对4T1肿瘤浸润免疫细胞进行scRNA-seq和流式分析，评估免疫微环境（TIME）的变化（如CD8+ T细胞、巨噬细胞极化）。 4. 体外共培养与机制验证：建立T细胞介导的肿瘤细胞杀伤实验，区分肌苷对T细胞和肿瘤细胞的直接作用；使用LiP-SMap化学蛋白质组学筛选肌苷结合蛋白；通过CRISPR筛选和基因敲除验证UBA6的功能。 5. 生化与分子机制：体外纯化UBA6和USE1蛋白，检测肌苷对UBA6-USE1相互作用及FAT10硫酯键形成的影响；通过RNA-seq和Western Blot分析UBA6缺失对炎症信号和抗原呈递的影响。 6. 临床相关性分析：利用TIDE数据库和自建的人体组织队列（食管癌、肺癌等），分析UBA6表达水平与ICB疗效、患者生存期及CD8+ T细胞浸润的关系。

contribution_and_limits.contribution: 识别出肌苷作为连接肠道微生物/代谢与ICB疗效的关键代谢物，并揭示其通过直接抑制肿瘤细胞UBA6来增强肿瘤内在免疫原性的新机制。
contribution_and_limits.limits: 所给摘要未交代肌苷在人体内的药代动力学细节及最佳给药剂量；所给摘要未交代肌苷对非嘌呤代谢途径或其他潜在脱靶效应的全面评估；临床验证队列规模较小（n=22用于IHC，部分公共数据），且缺乏对患者内源性肌苷水平的直接测量（因腺苷快速降解为肌苷，测量存在技术挑战）。

key_findings.conditions: B16-F0小鼠模型及人RCC患者队列
key_findings.finding: ICB治疗后血浆中嘌呤代谢物（包括肌苷）水平升高；在人RCC患者中，基线高水平肌苷与尼莫单抗（anti-PD1）治疗后的更长总生存期（mOS 33 vs 22个月）相关，但与mTOR抑制剂无关。

key_findings.conditions: B16-GMCSF和4T1小鼠模型（ICB抵抗模型）
key_findings.finding: 肌苷补充剂与ICB联合治疗克服了内在耐药性，显著延长生存期并诱导完全缓解；肌苷不引起系统性炎症或肝毒性。

key_findings.conditions: 4T1肿瘤微环境
key_findings.finding: 肌苷+ICB组合治疗将免疫抑制性TIME转化为炎症性TIME，增加M1型巨噬细胞、效应CD8+ T细胞比例，减少M2型巨噬细胞和Treg。

key_findings.conditions: 体外T细胞-肿瘤细胞共培养
key_findings.finding: 肌苷预处理肿瘤细胞而非T细胞，显著增强肿瘤细胞对T细胞介导的细胞毒性的敏感性；肌苷上调肿瘤细胞表面MHC-I表达及抗原加工/呈递相关基因。

key_findings.conditions: LiP-SMap筛选与CRISPR筛选
key_findings.finding: 肌苷直接结合并抑制UBA6活性；UBA6缺失使肿瘤细胞对T细胞和NK细胞介导的杀伤更敏感。

key_findings.conditions: UBA6功能缺失模型
key_findings.finding: UBA6缺失模拟肌苷效应，上调TNF-α、IFN响应基因及MHC-I表达；UBA6缺失消除了肌苷对基因表达的进一步诱导作用，表明肌苷通过抑制UBA6发挥作用。

key_findings.conditions: 不同肿瘤细胞系（MC38 vs 4T1/B16）
key_findings.finding: 肌苷仅在高表达UBA6的肿瘤细胞（4T1, B16）中增强免疫原性；在低表达UBA6的MC38细胞中无效，但在过表达UBA6的MC38细胞中恢复效应。

key_findings.conditions: 人类肿瘤队列（黑色素瘤、NSCLC等）
key_findings.finding: 肿瘤细胞中高UBA6表达与ICB治疗后的较差无进展生存期（PFS）和总生存期（OS）相关；低UBA6表达与较高的客观缓解率（ORR）和CD8+ T细胞浸润正相关。

study_summary_A.problem_or_question: 尽管免疫检查点阻断（ICB）疗法在某些癌症中取得显著成效，但大多数患者无响应或产生耐药性。肿瘤内在因素（如低突变负荷、局部免疫抑制）和宿主因素导致响应异质性。具体而言，肿瘤代谢环境的改变如何调节抗肿瘤免疫反应并影响ICB疗效？特别是肠道微生物群产生的代谢物是否通过特定分子机制直接作用于肿瘤细胞以克服内在耐药性？
study_summary_A.research_scope: 小鼠黑色素瘤（B16-F0, B16-GMCSF）和三阴性乳腺癌（4T1）模型，以及人类肾细胞癌（CheckMate 025队列）、黑色素瘤和实体瘤篮式试验患者队列。研究聚焦于免疫检查点阻断（ICB）治疗下的肿瘤代谢微环境与内在免疫原性。
study_summary_A.work_summary: 本研究旨在阐明肿瘤代谢状态如何影响免疫检查点阻断（ICB）的疗效。通过小鼠模型的代谢组学筛选和临床队列分析，发现嘌呤代谢物肌苷（inosine）水平与ICB敏感性正相关。机制研究表明，肌苷直接抑制肿瘤细胞内的泛素激活酶UBA6，从而增强肿瘤细胞的抗原呈递能力和对T细胞介导的细胞毒性的敏感性，进而改善抗肿瘤免疫反应。该通路在多种ICB抵抗的小鼠模型中验证了肌苷联合ICB的治疗潜力，并在人类肿瘤样本中证实了UBA6高表达与不良预后及低CD8+ T细胞浸润的相关性。

auxiliary_material: Mechanistic findings: Inosine directly inhibits UBA6 in tumour cells, enhancing tumour immunogenicity and sensitivity to T-cell-mediated killing.
Preclinical evidence: Inosine supplementation sensitizes intrinsically ICB-resistant mouse melanoma and breast cancer models to ICB by inflaming the tumour microenvironment.

Limitations stated by authors: The study did not validate or perform inosine measurement in their own clinical cohort of 22 patients due to intact sample issues; they relied on UBA6 expression as a proxy for the pathway's activity.
Technical context: Adenosine degrades rapidly into inosine (~10 s) and clears quickly, whereas inosine has a longer half-life (~15 h), which impacts measurement strategies in human plasma.
supplement_gap_material.outline_action: Search for studies that directly quantify inosine concentrations in human tumour biopsies or microdialysates. If only plasma data is available, clarify whether the gap requires intra-tumoral specificity or if systemic correlates are acceptable per the success criteria definition of 'tumour-adjacent material'. Note that this study provides strong associative evidence via plasma levels but lacks the direct intra-tumoral measurement required to fully satisfy the 'inside the human tumour microenvironment' criterion.
supplement_gap_material.remaining_gap: The specific measured concentration value of inosine inside the human tumour microenvironment (TME) is not provided. The study measures inosine in plasma (serum) of human RCC patients and in mouse plasma/tumours, but does not report direct quantification of inosine within the solid human tumour tissue itself. Furthermore, while the association between plasma inosine levels and survival is established, no absolute concentration values (e.g., ng/mL or μM) for human plasma or TME are explicitly stated in the text.
useful_material: The study identifies inosine as a purine metabolite associated with immune checkpoint blockade (ICB) sensitivity in both mouse models and human renal cell carcinoma (RCC) patients treated with nivolumab.

In human RCC patients from the CheckMate 025 trial, higher baseline plasma levels of inosine were significantly associated with longer overall survival (median OS 33 months vs. 22 months for low levels) specifically in the nivolumab-treated cohort.
The authors note that circulating inosine levels are influenced by gut microbiota dysbiosis induced by ICB treatment, as well as diet and genetics.
The study reports that plasma levels of inosine were reduced in both tumour-bearing mice and cancer patients after ICB treatment, suggesting dynamic changes during therapy.

source_materials.title: Inhibition of UBA6 by inosine augments tumour immunogenicity and responses

deep_read_material.paper_title: Fecal microbiota transplantation plus immunotherapy in non-small cell lung cancer and melanoma: the phase 2 FMT-LUMINate trial

examples.conditions: 研究人群：NSCLC队列（n=20，一线治疗，PD-L1 TPS ≥ 50%，无既往抗PD-1暴露）；黑色素瘤队列（n=20，一线治疗，允许既往辅助抗PD-1但需停药>6个月）。干预措施：单次健康供体粪便微生物移植（FMT，口服胶囊）后紧接着启动ICI治疗。NSCLC组使用帕博利珠单抗（pembrolizumab）单药；黑色素瘤组使用纳武利尤单抗（nivolumab）联合伊匹木单抗（ipilimumab）。
examples.finding: 在NSCLC队列中，FMT联合抗PD-1治疗的客观缓解率（ORR）为80%（16/20），超过了预设的64%主要终点阈值。在黑色素瘤队列中，FMT联合抗PD-1加抗CTLA-4（双ICI）治疗的ORR为75%（15/20）。关于毒性信号，在黑色素瘤双ICI组中观察到严重不良事件（AEs）的发生率较高且起病更早：13名患者（65%）经历了3级或更高级别的AEs，其中腹泻或结肠炎是最常见的3级及以上AE（20%的患者），另有15%的患者出现心肌炎。严重毒性的中位起病时间为开始抗PD-1和抗CTLA-4治疗后40天，早于文献报道的60天。相比之下，NSCLC单药抗PD-1组无3级或以上AEs发生。
examples.use_in_review: 提供FMT联合免疫检查点抑制剂（ICI）在非小细胞肺癌（NSCLC）和黑色素瘤中的具体客观缓解率（ORR），以及双免疫检查点抑制剂（dual ICI）治疗下的毒性信号特征。

question_material.explanation: 该研究通过FMT-LUMINate II期临床试验评估了FMT联合ICI在两种不同癌症背景下的临床活性与安全性。结果显示，FMT显著提高了NSCLC患者对单药抗PD-1治疗的反应率（80%），并改善了黑色素瘤患者对双免疫检查点阻断（抗PD-1+抗CTLA-4）的反应率（75%）。然而，在黑色素瘤双ICI背景下，FMT联合治疗伴随着更高的免疫相关不良事件（irAEs）风险，特别是心肌炎和早期发作的严重毒性。这种毒性信号与特定供体来源的微生物群（富含Prevotella spp.）有关，且仅在双ICI背景下出现，而在单药抗PD-1背景下未观察到类似毒性。这表明FMT的安全性与特定的ICI治疗方案及供体微生物特征存在交互作用。

broader_review_uses.connection_to_review: 为综述中关于“FMT作用机制的争议”提供反面证据或补充视角，即定植效率可能不是决定疗效的唯一或主要因素。
broader_review_uses.material: 研究指出FMT疗效不依赖于供体-宿主相似性或菌株水平定植，而是依赖于基线微生物组的整体重塑和有害菌清除。
broader_review_uses.purpose: 背景信息，用于对比不同研究中关于FMT机制的解释（定植vs清除）。

broader_review_uses.connection_to_review: 跨研究的一致性证据，支持“有害菌清除”作为FMT疗效通用机制的假设。
broader_review_uses.material: 提到TACITO试验也观察到类似的结果，即在FMT组中观察到基线物种的消除，而在安慰剂组中没有。
broader_review_uses.purpose: 作为外部验证，增强综述中关于机制结论的可信度。

facet_contributions.boundaries: 仅适用于未经过ICI治疗的原发性耐药患者；NSCLC结果基于高PD-L1表达人群；黑色素瘤结果包含不同BRAF状态。
facet_contributions.contribution: 提供了FMT联合ICI在NSCLC（抗PD-1）和黑色素瘤（抗PD-1/CTLA-4）中的具体ORR数据（分别为80%和75%），证明了其在一线治疗中提高临床活性的能力。
facet_contributions.possible_uses: 用于回答“肠道微生物群如何调节实体瘤中ICI的疗效”，提供具体的临床响应率证据，支持FMT作为增敏策略的有效性。

facet_contributions.boundaries: 机制主要在人类队列中通过相关性分析发现，并通过小鼠模型进行功能验证；不同肿瘤类型中富集的有益菌种类有限重叠，但有害菌清除模式一致。
facet_contributions.contribution: 阐明了FMT起效的潜在机制：响应者的获益主要依赖于基线有害细菌物种（如Enterocloster, Clostridium）的大量丢失，而非供体菌株的成功定植。这种丢失与血浆中色氨酸代谢产物（喹啉酸、犬尿氨酸）水平的降低以及效应性CD8+ T细胞的增加相关。动物实验证实，重新引入这些丢失的有害菌会阻断ICI疗效。
facet_contributions.possible_uses: 用于回答“介导该效应的机制是什么”，提供微生物组重塑的具体分子和免疫学路径，挑战传统的“益生菌定植”主导观点，强调“去致病化”的重要性。

facet_contributions.boundaries: 仅在黑色素瘤双免疫治疗队列中观察到显著的毒性信号；在NSCLC单药治疗或未使用双免疫治疗的既往研究中未观察到相同程度的毒性。
facet_contributions.contribution: 揭示了特定供体菌群特征（富含Prevotella spp.）与双免疫检查点抑制（抗PD-1/CTLA-4）背景下严重免疫相关不良反应（如心肌炎、早期发作的3级以上AEs）之间的关联。
facet_contributions.possible_uses: 用于讨论ICI疗效与安全性之间的权衡，以及微生物组在预测和管理irAEs中的作用，提示未来FMT研究中供体筛选的重要性。

review_planning_B.planning_summary: 该论文为综述提供了关于FMT联合ICI治疗实体瘤的关键临床数据，特别是其在克服原发性耐药方面的潜力。更重要的是，它提出了一个区别于传统“有益菌定植”假说的新机制框架：即治疗获益主要源于FMT诱导的基线有害病原体（pathobionts）的清除，进而调节宿主代谢和免疫微环境。此外，它还揭示了供体菌群特征（如Prevotella丰度）与特定ICI方案（双免疫检查点抑制）相互作用下的安全性风险。
scope_interpretation_cautions: 该研究的机制结论（有害菌清除导致疗效）是基于观察性关联和小鼠功能验证，需谨慎推断其在所有FMT场景下的普适性。
黑色素瘤队列中的严重毒性信号可能与双免疫检查点抑制的背景有关，不能直接外推至单药ICI治疗。
供体选择对毒性的影响提示个体化差异，但本研究未建立标准化的供体筛选算法，仅作为警示。
NSCLC队列的高ORR可能受限于高PD-L1表达人群的预后较好，需注意人群特异性。
topic_handles: FMT介导的微生物组重塑机制（有害菌清除 vs 有益菌定植）
肠道微生物-免疫代谢轴（色氨酸代谢, 喹啉酸, 犬尿氨酸）
ICI相关不良反应（irAEs）的微生物驱动因素
供体选择对治疗安全性和有效性的影响

study_summary_A.approach: 研究设计为前瞻性、多中心、单臂II期临床试验。入组标准包括：NSCLC患者需PD-L1 TPS ≥50%且无一线可操作基因改变；黑色素瘤患者不限BRAF状态。所有患者在开始ICI治疗前一周内接受来自健康供体的单次FMT（口服胶囊）。主要终点是NSCLC队列的ORR。次要终点包括黑色素瘤ORR、1年无进展生存期（PFS）、总生存期（OS）、疾病控制率（DCR）及安全性。微生物组分析采用鸟枪法宏基因组测序，结合定量PCR和高通量培养组学验证细菌变化。此外，通过血浆代谢组学和流式细胞术分析免疫代谢景观，并在抗生素处理的荷瘤小鼠模型中通过回输“丢失”的细菌混合物来验证因果机制。

contribution_and_limits.contribution: 提供了FMT联合ICI在NSCLC和黑色素瘤一线治疗中的临床活性证据，证实FMT可提高ORR。识别出“基线有害菌清除”作为潜在的药效学生物标志物，并揭示了其与色氨酸代谢抑制及CD8+ T细胞扩增的关联。
contribution_and_limits.limits: 研究为单臂设计，缺乏安慰剂对照，难以完全排除自然病程或其他混杂因素。样本量较小（每队列20人），限制了亚组分析和统计效力。黑色素瘤队列中观察到的严重毒性信号（如心肌炎）需要更大规模的随机试验进一步确认。供体选择对毒性的影响提示个体化差异，但具体筛选标准尚未确立。

key_findings.conditions: NSCLC患者接受FMT+抗PD-1
key_findings.finding: ORR达到80%（16/20），满足主要终点；1年OS为100%；未观察到3级及以上与治疗相关的不良事件。

key_findings.conditions: 黑色素瘤患者接受FMT+抗PD-1+抗CTLA-4
key_findings.finding: ORR为75%（15/20）；观察到较文献报道更早发生的严重免疫相关不良反应（irAEs），包括心肌炎；部分严重AEs与富含Prevotella的供体有关。

key_findings.conditions: 微生物组分析与临床响应关联
key_findings.finding: 响应者（R）与非响应者（NR）相比，在FMT后表现出显著更高的基线细菌物种丢失幅度。这种丢失主要由有害菌（如Enterocloster, Clostridium, Streptococcus）构成，而非供体菌株的定植。

key_findings.conditions: 机制验证（动物实验）
key_findings.finding: 在抗生素处理的小鼠中，将FMT响应者基线样本中丢失的有害细菌混合物重新引入，抵消了FMT联合ICI的抗肿瘤效应，证实消除有害菌是治疗获益的必要条件。

study_summary_A.problem_or_question: 尽管免疫检查点抑制剂改善了NSCLC和黑色素瘤的预后，但超过半数的患者存在原发性耐药。目前尚不清楚健康供体FMT联合抗PD-1（NSCLC）或抗PD-1联合抗CTLA-4（黑色素瘤）在一线治疗中的临床活性和安全性，以及FMT增强ICI疗效的人类机制。
study_summary_A.research_scope: 该研究针对晚期非小细胞肺癌（NSCLC）和皮肤黑色素瘤患者，评估健康供体粪便微生物群移植（FMT）联合一线免疫检查点抑制剂（ICI）治疗的临床疗效、安全性及机制。NSCLC队列接受抗PD-1单药治疗，黑色素瘤队列接受抗PD-1联合抗CTLA-4双免疫检查点抑制治疗。
study_summary_A.work_summary: 这是一项多中心、开放标签的II期临床试验（FMT-LUMINate），旨在评估单次口服胶囊FMT在启动ICI治疗前对原发性耐药患者的影响。研究纳入20名NSCLC患者和20名黑色素瘤患者。主要终点为NSCLC队列的客观缓解率（ORR）。结果显示，NSCLC队列ORR为80%，超过预设阈值；黑色素瘤队列ORR为75%。安全性方面，NSCLC组无3级及以上不良事件，而黑色素瘤组出现较早发的严重免疫相关不良反应（irAEs），特别是心肌炎，且与特定供体菌群有关。机制研究发现，响应者并非通过获得特定的供体菌株定植获益，而是通过显著清除基线存在的有害细菌物种（如Enterocloster和Clostridium属），从而降低色氨酸代谢途径活性并改善全身免疫微环境。

supplement_gap_material.auxiliary_material: The authors explicitly state that this is a phase 2 trial, not a phase 3 trial. They mention that the findings will be assessed as part of the CanBiome2 randomized trial (NCT06623461), which is described as a randomized trial evaluating FMT in combination with ICI in 128 patients, but the current paper does not report the results of this phase 3 trial. The study design was open-label and single-arm for the cohorts reported here, lacking the randomization required for a phase 3 RCT status.
supplement_gap_material.outline_action: Search for published results from the CanBiome2 trial (NCT06623461) or other large-scale randomized phase III trials of microbiome interventions in ICI-treated cancer patients to determine if any have been completed and reported since this publication.
supplement_gap_material.remaining_gap: The gap requires evidence of a completed large randomised phase III trial. This material provides only a phase 2 trial. While the authors reference an ongoing/forthcoming phase 3 trial (CanBiome2), they do not provide its results or confirm its completion within this text.
supplement_gap_material.useful_material: This study reports the results of FMT-LUMINate, a multicenter, open-label, phase 2 trial evaluating healthy donor fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) combined with immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICI) in patients with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) or melanoma. The trial enrolled 40 patients (20 NSCLC, 20 melanoma). In the NSCLC cohort receiving anti-PD-1 monotherapy, the objective response rate (ORR) was 80%. In the melanoma cohort receiving dual anti-PD-1 and anti-CTLA-4 therapy, the ORR was 75%. The study found that clinical response was associated with the loss of baseline deleterious bacterial species rather than the engraftment of donor-specific strains. Safety data indicated no grade 3+ adverse events in the NSCLC cohort, but a higher incidence of severe immune-related adverse events (including myocarditis) in the melanoma cohort, particularly among recipients of donors rich in Prevotella spp.

review_planning_B.planning_summary: [REDACTED_ORIGINAL_PASSAGE; DOI/source identity retained elsewhere] 肌苷 (Inosine) UBA6 (Ubiquitin-like modifier activating enzyme 6)

source_materials.title: Inhibiting tumor cell-intrinsic UBA6 by inosine augments tumor immunogenicity

broader_review_uses.connection_to_review: 提供了肌苷在肠道稳态中的基础作用背景，即其正常局限于肠腔并通过A2A受体维持屏障和免疫耐受，这为理解其在CRC中因屏障破坏而进入组织层后的功能转变提供了对比基线。
broader_review_uses.material: 肌苷在生理状态下由共生菌产生，维持上皮紧密连接蛋白表达，抑制NF-κB/Nrf2通路，减少氧化应激和炎症。
broader_review_uses.purpose: 作为背景信息，说明微生物代谢物功能的语境依赖性，强调病理状态（如CRC）下空间分布改变是功能重编程的前提。

broader_review_uses.connection_to_review: 介绍了肌苷来源的多样性，包括特定细菌菌株（Bifidobacterium pseudolongum, Lactobacillus johnsonii等）及宿主酶（ADA, LACC1），以及饮食和宿主代谢的贡献。
broader_review_uses.material: 列举了多种产肌苷菌属，并指出Akkermansia muciniphila间接影响肌苷可用性；描述了肌苷的化学稳定性和受体亲和力。
broader_review_uses.purpose: 用于分类讨论不同微生物来源对代谢物池的贡献，以及宿主-微生物共同调控网络，有助于理解个体间微生物组差异可能导致的代谢物水平变异。

broader_review_uses.connection_to_review: 探讨了基于肌苷的治疗策略，包括外源性补充和工程益生菌，并指出了转化医学中的挑战，如菌株定植、安全性、药代动力学和监管障碍。
broader_review_uses.material: 提到工程菌降解腺苷生成肌苷以增强T细胞浸润；指出当前临床数据有限，尤其是CRC特异性数据缺失；强调安全问题和监管挑战。
broader_review_uses.purpose: 作为未来研究方向和实践知识的来源，提示在评估微生物疗法时需要考虑的实际障碍，避免过度乐观地解读前临床结果。

facet_contributions.boundaries: 主要基于小鼠模型（MC38, CT26等）和混合肿瘤人群的II期试验，缺乏大规模、专门针对CRC患者的随机对照试验数据来确证其对ICI疗效的显著提升；临床数据中CRC亚组样本量小且未单独报告。
facet_contributions.contribution: 提供了肌苷通过激活T细胞（特别是Th1分化）和促进巨噬细胞M1极化来增强抗肿瘤免疫的具体机制，并引用了前临床模型中肌苷协同ICI治疗减少肿瘤生长的证据。还提及了一项混合实体瘤II期临床试验中肌苷辅助ICI治疗的初步积极结果。
facet_contributions.possible_uses: 用于回答肠道微生物群如何调节固体肿瘤中ICI疗效的问题，具体机制涉及微生物代谢物直接激活效应T细胞和重塑髓系细胞表型。可用于举例说明微生物代谢物作为生物标志物或治疗增敏剂的潜力。

facet_contributions.boundaries: 机制细节多来自体外细胞系（SW480, HT29）和小鼠模型；人体组织中肌苷的具体浓度梯度、受体表达谱及其与ICI疗效的直接相关性尚未完全阐明；肌苷的促癌作用（EMT、代谢支持）提示其并非在所有情况下都有益，需结合具体情境判断。
facet_contributions.contribution: 详细阐述了肌苷介导ICI疗效增强的分子机制：1) 通过A2A受体激活CD8+ T细胞和Th1细胞，增加IFN-γ释放；2) 促进巨噬细胞向M1样促炎表型极化（增加CD86和iNOS）；3) 工程菌将腺苷转化为肌苷以减少免疫抑制微环境。同时指出肌苷也可被肿瘤细胞用作碳源或通过LACC1促进EMT，体现其双重性。
facet_contributions.possible_uses: 用于深入解释微生物代谢物调节ICI疗效的具体细胞和分子机制，特别是T细胞耗竭的逆转和髓系细胞的再教育。可用于讨论代谢竞争（肿瘤细胞 vs T细胞利用肌苷）对免疫治疗结果的潜在负面影响，丰富对机制复杂性的理解。

review_planning_B.planning_summary: 该综述提供了肌苷作为连接肠道微生物群与免疫检查点抑制剂（ICI）疗效的关键代谢物的详细机制解释。它特别适用于阐述微生物代谢物如何通过调节T细胞功能和巨噬细胞极化来增强固体肿瘤中对ICIs的反应，同时也提供了关于代谢物在肿瘤微环境中时空分布变化的重要背景，有助于解释为何某些代谢物能改善免疫治疗结局。
scope_interpretation_cautions: 该综述的核心贡献在于概念整合和机制梳理，而非提供新的实证数据。其关于肌苷在CRC中作用的结论主要基于前临床模型和有限的混合肿瘤临床数据，不能直接外推为CRC患者的标准治疗建议。
肌苷在CRC中具有双重作用（促癌和抗瘤），其净效应取决于疾病阶段、空间分布和微环境组成。在规划综述时，应避免简单地将肌苷归类为‘好’或‘坏’的代谢物，而应强调其语境依赖性。
引用的II期临床试验结果来自混合实体瘤人群，其中CRC患者仅占少数且未单独分析，因此不能据此断定肌苷对CRC患者ICI疗效的确切影响。
文中提到的‘时空重编程’是一个概念框架，目前缺乏人类纵向数据直接验证肌苷水平从结肠炎到CRC的动态变化轨迹，部分推断基于动物模型和相关疾病的间接证据。
topic_handles: T cell activation via A2A receptor
LACC1-mediated inosine production in tumor cells

study_summary_A.approach: 采用系统性文献回顾方法，检索PubMed数据库中关于肌苷、嘌呤代谢、肠道微生物群、肠道稳态及结直肠癌的相关研究。筛选标准包括同行评审的英文文章，优先选择提供机制或功能见解的前临床（体外/体内）研究，以弥补临床数据的不足；同时纳入相关条件（如IBD、实验性结肠炎）的研究以 contextualize 肌苷在炎症驱动致癌中的作用。通过综合生化特性、信号通路、空间分布变化、时间动态演变及免疫调节机制，构建肌苷在CRC发展中“时空重编程”的概念模型。

contribution_and_limits.contribution: 提出了肌苷在CRC发展中“时空重编程”的概念，整合了其从稳态维持到促癌代谢底物再到免疫调节剂的多重角色，解释了其在不同情境下的矛盾效应。
contribution_and_limits.limits: 主要依赖前临床数据和有限的混合肿瘤临床数据，缺乏针对CRC患者肌苷水平的纵向追踪研究；工程菌疗法的安全性和定植稳定性尚不明确；未提供具体的剂量-效应关系或人群特异性预测指标。

key_findings.conditions: 生理状态/肠道稳态
key_findings.finding: 肌苷主要由肠道菌群（如Bifidobacterium pseudolongum, Lactobacillus spp.）和宿主产生，局限于肠腔，通过A2A受体支持上皮屏障完整性，抑制促炎细胞因子，维持免疫耐受。

key_findings.conditions: CRC进展期/肿瘤微环境
key_findings.finding: 肌苷发生空间重分布进入组织层，并在时间上呈现双重作用：一方面被肿瘤细胞利用作为替代碳源并促进EMT（通过TGF-β1/LACC1通路），具有促癌效应；另一方面通过激活T细胞（Th1分化）和促进巨噬细胞M1极化，增强抗肿瘤免疫反应。

key_findings.conditions: 免疫检查点抑制剂（ICI）治疗背景
key_findings.finding: 前临床模型显示，肌苷可协同PD-1/CTLA-4阻断疗法，增加肿瘤浸润淋巴细胞和IFN-γ水平，提高疗效。一项包含CRC患者的II期临床试验初步表明联合肌苷可轻微增强ICI疗效并降低毒性，但缺乏CRC特异性亚组分析。

study_summary_A.problem_or_question: 旨在解决肌苷这一曾被忽视的嘌呤代谢物在肠道健康与疾病（特别是CRC）中功能复杂且看似矛盾的角色问题，阐明其如何随病理进程发生时空重编程，从而为理解微生物-宿主互作及开发新型微生物疗法提供理论框架。
study_summary_A.research_scope: 肠道微生物代谢物肌苷（inosine）在肠道稳态维持及结直肠癌（CRC）发生发展中的时空重编程作用，涵盖其生化特性、来源、信号通路、对上皮屏障和免疫系统的调节，以及在肿瘤微环境中的双重角色。
study_summary_A.work_summary: 本文是一篇综述，系统梳理了肌苷作为关键微生物代谢物的生物学功能及其在从肠道稳态向结直肠癌转变过程中的动态变化。文章首先介绍了肌苷的化学性质、主要来源（宿主酶促反应及特定肠道菌群如双歧杆菌、乳酸菌等）及其通过腺苷受体介导的信号通路。随后，阐述了肌苷在生理状态下对肠道上皮屏障完整性和黏膜免疫耐受的支持作用。重点讨论了在慢性炎症和CRC背景下，肌苷的空间分布从肠腔向组织层的转移，以及时间维度上从抗炎稳态维持者向促进肿瘤细胞侵袭和代谢适应的促癌因子，同时兼具增强抗肿瘤免疫（如T细胞激活、巨噬细胞极化）的双重复杂角色。最后，评估了基于肌苷轴的临床治疗潜力，包括补充外源性肌苷和使用工程菌策略，并指出了当前临床证据有限及转化面临的挑战。

supplement_gap_material.auxiliary_material: The study describes the biochemical properties of inosine, its sources (including Bifidobacterium pseudolongum and host enzymes like ADA and LACC1), and its role in gut homeostasis versus colorectal cancer (CRC) progression. It outlines preclinical evidence from mouse models (MC38, CT26) showing inosine's dual role in supporting tumor cell metabolism under glucose restriction while simultaneously enhancing anti-tumor immunity. The text also notes that SCFAs are more extensively studied than purine metabolites but does not elaborate on SCFA concentrations.
supplement_gap_material.outline_action: Future planning should prioritize locating primary clinical metabolomic studies or datasets that specifically quantify inosine and SCFA levels in human CRC patients undergoing immunotherapy, rather than relying on review summaries. Investigators should examine the primary references cited in this review (e.g., the Phase-2 trial reference [47] and metabolomic studies [40-42]) to determine if raw concentration data exists there, even if not summarized in this text. Additionally, searches should target 'metabolomics,' 'biomarker,' and 'pharmacokinetics' in the context of ICI-treated CRC cohorts to find the missing quantitative correlations.
supplement_gap_material.remaining_gap: The supplied material does not contain quantitative physiological concentrations (e.g., μM, ng/mL) of inosine or SCFAs measured in human tumour tissue or serum that are correlated with ICI response outcomes. The authors explicitly indicate that studies reporting spatial redistribution of inosine in human CRC compartments are missing and that no human studies have longitudinally tracked inosine levels from colitis to CRC. Consequently, the specific biomarker data required to establish a correlation between endogenous metabolite levels and clinical response remains unavailable in this text.
supplement_gap_material.useful_material: The authors provide a detailed mechanistic explanation of how inosine modulates immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) response, specifically through adenosine A2A receptor-dependent activation of CD8+ T cells and Th1 differentiation, and promotion of M1-like macrophage polarization. The text references a Phase-2 clinical trial where inosine supplementation (0.2 g orally three times/day) was combined with PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitors and chemotherapy in a mixed solid-tumor population, noting a mild enhancement of efficacy, though CRC-specific outcomes were not separately reported. Crucially, the authors explicitly state that human data regarding spatial redistribution and quantitative levels of inosine in CRC are currently missing or under-characterized compared to other metabolites like short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs), confirming the scarcity of the requested data type.

source_materials.title: From Gut Homeostasis to Colorectal Cancer: Spatial and Temporal Reprogramming of Microbial Inosine Signaling

broader_review_uses.connection_to_review: Helps explain why inosine might be a more effective endogenous or supplemented mediator than adenosine in the tumor microenvironment, influencing the rationale for studying its role in ICI response.
broader_review_uses.material: Inosine has a much longer half-life (15 h) compared to adenosine (~5 s), allowing it to act as a stable signaling molecule. It is produced by adenosine deaminase (ADA) and gut microbiota.
broader_review_uses.purpose: Contextual background on purine metabolism and inosine stability

broader_review_uses.connection_to_review: Clarifies that the observed benefits in cancer and other diseases may not be solely due to hyperuricemia, supporting the investigation of direct inosine-microbiome-immune interactions.
broader_review_uses.material: Historically, inosine's benefits were attributed to its downstream product, uric acid. However, recent studies show inosine itself has direct protective and immunomodulatory effects independent of urate.
broader_review_uses.purpose: Comparison of inosine vs. urate effects

facet_contributions.boundaries: Evidence is primarily from mouse models (gnotobiotic mice, DSS-induced colitis model). Human validation of this specific bacterial strain's role in ICI response is not established in this text.
facet_contributions.contribution: Identifies Bifidobacterium pseudolongum as an inosine-producing gut bacterium that enhances the efficacy of anticancer immunotherapy in mice. Describes the association between gut microbiota composition and inosine levels in the tumor microenvironment.
facet_contributions.possible_uses: Supports the argument that specific gut microbes can modulate ICI efficacy by producing metabolites like inosine. Provides a concrete example of a microbial mechanism affecting solid tumor outcomes.

facet_contributions.boundaries: Mechanistic details are derived from animal and cell culture studies. The text notes that while inosine has similar properties to adenosine, its longer half-life makes it distinct. Direct causal proof in humans is lacking.
facet_contributions.contribution: Details the mechanism: microbiota-derived inosine acts through adenosine 2A receptors (A2aR) on T lymphocytes infiltrating tumors. Also notes inosine serves as a carbon source for T-cell metabolism in glucose-restricted environments.
facet_contributions.possible_uses: Directly addresses the mechanistic question of how gut-derived metabolites influence immune cells. Explains the receptor-level interaction (A2aR) and metabolic support (carbon source) for T-cell function in the tumor microenvironment.

review_planning_B.planning_summary: This review provides crucial mechanistic insights into how gut microbiota-derived inosine modulates the tumor microenvironment and enhances immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) efficacy, a key topic for the review plan. It details the pathway where specific bacteria produce inosine, which then acts on T-cell adenosine receptors to improve anti-tumor immunity. Additionally, it highlights the metabolic link between inosine, adipose tissue browning, and energy expenditure, offering context for host-microbiome interactions in solid tumors.
scope_interpretation_cautions: The review explicitly states that human studies on inosine's direct effects (beyond urate elevation) are limited. Do not extrapolate animal/cell findings of direct anti-tumor or anti-inflammatory effects to humans without noting this gap.

The connection between gut microbiota-derived inosine and ICI efficacy is demonstrated in mouse models. Caution is needed when applying this mechanism to human patients, as human microbiome compositions and responses may differ.

While the review mentions inosine's role in obesity and energy expenditure, this is separate from the cancer/immunology focus. Ensure the distinction between metabolic and immunological roles is maintained if both are relevant to the broader review.
topic_handles: adipose tissue browning and energy expenditure

study_summary_A.approach: The authors conducted a narrative literature search using specific keywords (e.g., "inosine", "purine receptors") across UNC Health Sciences Library, PubMed, and Google Scholar without year restrictions. Articles were selected based on the significance of results in clinical, animal, and cell culture studies, with critical assessment of methodological quality and limitations. Related review articles were included to integrate missing information. The synthesis is organized by source of evidence (animal, cell culture, human) and disease context.

contribution_and_limits.contribution: Provides a comprehensive synthesis of inosine's metabolic pathways, receptor interactions (A1, A2A, A2B, A3), and roles in diverse disease contexts (cancer, metabolic, neurological).
contribution_and_limits.limits: As a narrative review, it does not perform a systematic meta-analysis. The translation of preclinical mechanisms to humans remains unverified; human data is insufficient to confirm direct therapeutic effects independent of urate elevation.

key_findings.conditions: Animal models (mice/rats) and cell cultures
key_findings.finding: Inosine demonstrates anti-inflammatory, immunomodulatory, and neuroprotective properties. It increases energy expenditure, promotes browning of adipose tissue, improves leptin sensitivity, and enhances the efficacy of immune checkpoint blockade therapy in tumors via interaction with T-cells.

key_findings.conditions: Human clinical trials and cohort studies
key_findings.finding: Current human evidence is largely restricted to inosine's capacity to elevate serum urate concentrations to optimal levels (6-7 mg/dL) safely. No human studies have directly investigated its effects on energy expenditure, inflammation, or neuronal function beyond urate elevation.

study_summary_A.problem_or_question: To evaluate the current state of knowledge regarding the metabolic and therapeutic effects of inosine in complex diseases, specifically addressing the discrepancy between promising preclinical results and limited human clinical data, and to identify mechanisms and future research directions.
study_summary_A.research_scope: The paper reviews the metabolic role of inosine, a purine nucleoside, across various complex diseases including obesity, type 2 diabetes, cancers, cardiovascular diseases, and neurodegenerative disorders. It synthesizes evidence from animal models (rodents, non-human primates), cell culture studies, and human clinical trials/cohort studies.
study_summary_A.work_summary: This narrative review discusses the multifaceted biological effects of inosine, highlighting its potential as a therapeutic agent for complex diseases. The authors summarize how inosine, derived from adenosine deamination or gut microbiota, exerts anti-inflammatory, immunomodulatory, neuroprotective, and metabolic benefits. While animal and cell studies demonstrate direct physiological effects such as increased energy expenditure and tumor immune response enhancement, human evidence is currently limited primarily to inosine's ability to safely elevate serum urate levels. The review identifies significant gaps in translating these preclinical findings to human applications, particularly regarding inflammation, oxidative stress, and neuronal function.

supplement_gap_material.auxiliary_material: The text summarizes human clinical trials where inosine was used to elevate serum urate in neurodegenerative diseases (Parkinson's, ALS, Multiple Sclerosis), demonstrating safety and tolerability of inosine supplementation in humans up to 3 g/d, though these studies did not measure tumor concentrations or ICI response. It reports animal model data (Mager et al., 2020) showing inosine concentration was highest in the duodenum and overabundant in sera of mice mono-colonized with B. pseudolongum, but notes these findings have not yet been translated to human tumor measurements. The review also lists genetic variants in inosine transporters (ENT1) associated with body composition in humans, offering potential covariates for future human studies.

Cite the explicit statement regarding the lack of human tumor concentration data to reinforce the gap's significance. Search for the primary references cited for the mouse immunotherapy data (e.g., Mager et al., Science 2020) to verify if any human cohort analysis was omitted in this review. Prioritize searching clinical trial registries or metabolomic datasets from ICI trials that may have measured purine metabolites in biofluids or tissue biopsies.
supplement_gap_material.remaining_gap: The specific success criterion of identifying prospective human studies reporting absolute concentrations (e.g., μmol/g or μM) of inosine or SCFAs in paired tumor tissue and serum/stool from ICI-treated solid tumor patients remains unaddressed. This study explicitly states that human studies on inosine have been limited to urate-elevating properties and that findings from animal models regarding immunotherapy efficacy need to be translated to humans. No quantitative data on intratumoral inosine levels in cancer patients correlating with ICI response is provided.
supplement_gap_material.useful_material: This study details the mechanistic pathway by which gut microbiota-derived inosine enhances immune checkpoint inhibition (ICI) efficacy, specifically identifying Bifidobacterium pseudolongum as an inosine-producing bacterium that acts through adenosine A2A receptors on tumor-infiltrating T lymphocytes. It explains that inosine serves as an alternative carbon source for CD8+ T-cell function under glucose restriction and has a significantly longer half-life (15 h) than adenosine (~5 s), making it a stable signaling molecule in the microenvironment. The authors distinguish inosine's direct immunomodulatory effects from downstream urate effects, providing a biological rationale for quantifying inosine specifically rather than general purine metabolites.

broader_review_uses.connection_to_review: 提供背景信息和领域现状
broader_review_uses.material: 介绍了肠道微生物群的基本组成、多样性影响因素（饮食、抗生素、年龄等）及其在维持免疫稳态中的基础作用；讨论了当前临床转化的挑战（标准化、监管、安全性、个体差异）。
broader_review_uses.purpose: 用于综述的引言或背景部分，定义关键概念，阐述研究领域的复杂性和当前面临的障碍，为后续深入探讨机制和疗效提供语境。

broader_review_uses.connection_to_review: 提供干预策略的比较素材
broader_review_uses.material: 分别评估了饮食干预（高纤维、生酮）、益生菌（单一菌株vs多菌株）、益生元、抗生素（清除vs利用）和FMT在优化ICIs疗效方面的证据和案例（如MRx0518试验，NCT编号等）。
broader_review_uses.purpose: 用于综述中讨论“如何改善ICIs疗效”的部分。可作为不同干预手段优缺点、实施难度及临床进展的比较基准。

broader_review_uses.connection_to_review: 提供反例或复杂性证据
broader_review_uses.material: 指出SCFAs在不同治疗背景下（抗PD-1 vs 抗CTLA-4）可能有相反的效果；某些有益菌在其他情境下可能无关甚至有害；抗生素通常有害但特定情况下可能有益。
broader_review_uses.purpose: 用于强调GM-免疫相互作用的复杂性和情境依赖性，避免过度简化的结论，支持综述中关于“精准医疗”和“个性化干预”必要性的论点。

facet_contributions.boundaries: 关联多为观察性研究结果，存在队列异质性；不同癌症类型中相同菌群的作用可能不同；代谢物的具体阈值和时空动态未在单篇综述中明确界定。
facet_contributions.contribution: 提供了肠道微生物群组成变化与ICIs疗效（响应/耐药）及毒性（irAEs）之间关联的具体临床证据。列举了在不同实体瘤（如黑色素瘤、NSCLC、肾癌）中与良好预后相关的特定菌群（如Bifidobacterium, Akkermansia, Faecalibacterium）以及与不良预后或毒性相关的菌群。还指出了代谢物（如SCFAs）水平的双重作用。
facet_contributions.possible_uses: 用于回答“肠道微生物群如何调节ICIs疗效”中的相关性证据部分。可用于构建“菌群特征-治疗响应”的映射关系，或作为讨论个体差异来源的依据。

facet_contributions.boundaries: 许多机制细节源自小鼠模型（如无菌鼠、人源化小鼠），在人体内的确切验证程度有限；作者指出某些关联的确切机制“尚未完全揭示”；不同机制间可能存在复杂的交互作用，综述未提供定量整合模型。
facet_contributions.contribution: 详细阐述了GM调节ICIs疗效的潜在分子机制。包括：1) 特定细菌（如Bifidobacterium）通过激活树突状细胞（DCs）促进CD8+ T细胞致敏和浸润；2) 代谢物（如SCFAs、肌苷）通过表观遗传修饰（HDAC抑制）、受体激活（GPCRs, A2ARs）调节T细胞功能和分化；3) 菌群失调导致的肠屏障破坏引发全身炎症，影响免疫环境。
facet_contributions.possible_uses: 用于回答“哪些机制介导了这种效应”。提供具体的信号通路、细胞互作和代谢途径，支持对因果关系的理论解释。

review_planning_B.planning_summary: 该综述为“肠道微生物群如何调节实体瘤免疫检查点抑制剂疗效及机制”这一主题提供了详尽的背景、机制解释和临床证据汇总。它特别适合作为解释GM-免疫轴生物学基础的核心素材，以及用于对比不同干预策略（如FMT vs 益生菌 vs 饮食）有效性与局限性的参考。文中提供的具体菌株、代谢物和临床试验信息可直接用于构建证据图谱。
scope_interpretation_cautions: 该综述涵盖多种癌症类型（黑色素瘤、肺癌、肾癌、肝癌等），在应用其发现时需注意癌症类型的特异性，不能将所有实体瘤的结果一概而论。
文中提到的机制很多基于前临床模型（小鼠），在推断人体机制时需保持谨慎，区分动物实验结果与临床验证结果。
临床证据主要来自回顾性队列或小规模前瞻性研究，存在选择偏倚和混杂因素（如合并用药、饮食记录缺失），关联不等于因果。
干预措施（如益生菌、FMT）的效果高度依赖于供体/菌株特异性、给药时机和患者基线菌群状态，综述中的成功案例不代表普遍适用性。
topic_handles: Gut microbiota composition (Taxa: Bifidobacterium, Akkermansia, Faecalibacterium, Bacteroides)
Intervention strategies (FMT, Probiotics, Prebiotics, Diet, Antibiotics)
Mechanisms (DC activation, CD8+ T cell priming, HDAC inhibition, GPCR signaling)

study_summary_A.approach: 作为一篇综述，本研究采用文献综合方法。通过检索PubMed、Web of Science等多个数据库（截至2026年5月），筛选关于肠道微生物群、系统性免疫、免疫检查点抑制剂及癌症治疗的文献。内容组织逻辑为：1. GM基础与抗肿瘤功能概述；2. GM调节系统性免疫的机制（包括代谢物作用、免疫细胞分化）；3. GM对ICIs疗效及毒性的具体影响（分前临床和临床研究）；4. 基于GM的干预策略（饮食、益生菌、益生元、抗生素、FMT）；5. 未来展望与挑战。文中引用了大量具体的菌株、代谢物、受体通路及临床试验ID作为支撑材料。

contribution_and_limits.contribution: 提供了肠道微生物群调节ICIs疗效的系统性机制框架，涵盖了从菌群组成、代谢物信号到免疫细胞互作的多层次联系；汇总了针对多种实体瘤（黑色素瘤、NSCLC、肾癌等）的临床队列数据，识别了潜在的预测性生物标志物；全面评估了五种主要GM调控策略（饮食、益生菌、益生元、抗生素、FMT）的证据等级及临床应用现状。
contribution_and_limits.limits: 作为综述，其结论依赖于已发表研究的异质性结果，不同研究间菌群特征与疗效关联存在不一致性（如某些菌在不同癌症类型中作用相反）；许多机制仍基于动物模型，人体内的因果链条尚未完全确立；缺乏标准化的微生物组分析协议和临床干预方案，限制了结果的直接外推和临床转化；未提供新的原始实验数据。

key_findings.conditions: 抗PD-1/PD-L1治疗背景下
key_findings.finding: 有益菌群（如Bifidobacterium, Akkermansia muciniphila, Collinsella aerofaciens）的富集与更好的客观缓解率和生存期相关；其机制涉及激活树突状细胞、促进CD8+ T细胞浸润及产生IL-12。相反，某些菌群（如部分Bacteroides）或与耐药相关。

key_findings.conditions: 抗CTLA-4（Ipilimumab）治疗背景下
key_findings.finding: 厚壁菌门（Firmicutes），特别是Faecalibacterium属，与较好的治疗响应相关；而拟杆菌门（Bacteroidetes）的某些物种可能与较差预后或结肠炎毒性相关。

key_findings.conditions: 代谢物介导机制
key_findings.finding: 短链脂肪酸（SCFAs，如丁酸盐、丙酸盐）可通过抑制组蛋白去乙酰化酶（HDAC）或激活GPCR来调节Treg/Th17平衡及T细胞功能，但其作用具有情境依赖性（如在抗PD-1中可能有益，而在抗CTLA-4中高血清水平可能预示不良预后）。肌苷（Inosine）可激活T细胞腺苷A2A受体增强ICI疗效。

key_findings.conditions: 干预措施效果
key_findings.finding: FMT从ICI响应者转移至非响应者小鼠或患者，可恢复对PD-1阻断的敏感性；特定益生菌（如Bifidobacterium pseudolongum）或益生元（如菊粉）可增强抗肿瘤免疫；广谱抗生素通常损害ICI疗效，但特定抗生素（如万古霉素）在某些模型中可能有益。

study_summary_A.problem_or_question: 肠道微生物群如何通过其组成和代谢产物调节宿主系统性免疫，进而决定癌症免疫检查点抑制剂（ICIs）的治疗响应率、耐药性及毒性？有哪些基于GM的干预策略可以优化免疫治疗效果？
study_summary_A.research_scope: 人类肠道微生物群（GM）与系统性免疫反应及癌症免疫治疗（特别是免疫检查点抑制剂，ICIs）之间的相互作用。涵盖从基础机制到临床转化及干预策略的综合讨论。
study_summary_A.work_summary: 本文是一篇综述，旨在系统梳理肠道微生物群如何调节全身免疫系统并影响癌症免疫治疗的疗效与毒性。文章首先概述了GM的组成及其在维持免疫稳态中的作用，随后深入探讨了GM通过特定菌群（如双歧杆菌、阿克曼氏菌等）及其代谢产物（如短链脂肪酸、肌苷、胆汁酸）调节T细胞、树突状细胞等免疫细胞功能，进而影响肿瘤微环境的机制。接着，文章总结了前临床（小鼠模型）和临床研究证据，展示了GM组成与ICI（抗PD-1/PD-L1、抗CTLA-4）疗效及免疫相关不良反应（irAEs）的相关性。最后，文章评估了通过饮食干预、益生菌、益生元、抗生素及粪便微生物移植（FMT）等GM调控手段优化免疫治疗效果的潜力与挑战。

They summarize intervention strategies such as fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT), probiotics, and dietary modulation (high-fiber, ketogenic) aimed at optimizing ICI outcomes. The text also outlines clinical challenges including standardization, regulatory issues, and inter-individual variability in microbiome studies. Several clinical trial identifiers (NCT numbers) are listed for ongoing or completed trials assessing microbiome impact on immunotherapy.

Conduct a targeted search for prospective human studies specifically measuring intratumoral metabolite concentrations in ICI-treated patients. supplement_gap_material.remaining_gap: This study does not report the absolute physiological concentrations (e.g., μmol/g or μM) of inosine or SCFAs required by the success criteria. It references external primary studies for metabolite associations but does not reproduce the specific quantitative data. Furthermore, while it mentions metabolites propagating to tumor sites, it does not confirm measured concentrations within human tumor tissue itself; the inosine finding is explicitly linked to mouse models in the preclinical section. The text does not specify whether the cited human metabolite studies (Botticelli, Coutzac) were prospective or if they utilized paired tumor tissue and serum/stool sampling.
supplement_gap_material.useful_material: This study identifies inosine and short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) as key microbiota-derived metabolites influencing immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) response. It reports that Bifidobacterium pseudolongum-derived inosine improves antitumor actions via activation of adenosine A2A receptors on T cells, citing preclinical evidence (Mager et al. 2020). For SCFAs, it notes that increased fecal propionic acid in anti-PD-1 patients correlates with increased antitumor responses and prolonged survival (Botticelli et al. 2020), while increased serum butyrate in anti-CTLA-4 patients links to poor outcomes (Coutzac et al. 2020a, b). Mechanisms described include SCFA-mediated histone deacetylase (HDAC) suppression and G protein-coupled receptor (GPCR) activation. The text distinguishes between metabolite effects in different treatment contexts (anti-PD-1 vs. anti-CTLA-4) and compartments (fecal vs. serum).

source_materials.title: Gut microbiota modulation of systemic immunity and cancer immunotherapy: mechanisms, evidence, and therapeutic implications

broader_review_uses.connection_to_review: 用于说明当前领域的局限性、未来研究方向（标准化、大样本RCT、多中心合作）以及为何需要更严谨的综合分析。
broader_review_uses.material: 综述指出当前证据多为中等或低确定性，方法学异质性大（采样、测序、终点定义不一），缺乏标准化和高确定性RCT证据。黑色素瘤研究占主导，其他肿瘤类型（如血液瘤、胃肠道癌）研究不足。
broader_review_uses.purpose: 背景与领域现状

broader_review_uses.connection_to_review: 可作为评估不同微生物干预策略相对价值的定性比较框架，帮助读者理解不同干预手段在现有证据下的整体趋势。
broader_review_uses.material: 提出了“跨干预措施元效应评分”这一概念，将FMT、高纤维饮食、Vidutolimod评为正向（+1.0），抗生素、益生菌评为负向（-1.0）。
broader_review_uses.purpose: 概念框架与比较基准

broader_review_uses.connection_to_review: 用于讨论微生物疗法临床转化的实际障碍、监管环境和临床实践建议，超越单纯的科学发现，涵盖实施科学层面。
broader_review_uses.material: 讨论了FMT的伦理和监管挑战（病原体传播、长期效应、供体选择），以及EMA/FDA指南的不完善。建议优化抗生素使用，避免非靶向益生菌。
broader_review_uses.purpose: 实践启示与监管考量

facet_contributions.boundaries: 多数为观察性关联，因果方向需谨慎解读；黑色素瘤数据最多，其他肿瘤类型证据较弱；干预性研究（如FMT）样本量小，存在偏倚风险。
facet_contributions.contribution: 提供了肠道微生物群特征（多样性、特定菌属丰度）与ICI疗效（ORR, PFS, OS）之间关联的大量临床观察证据。明确了高多样性和有益菌富集与良好预后的正相关，以及抗生素/益生菌使用的负相关。
facet_contributions.possible_uses: 用于回答“肠道微生物群如何调节ICI疗效”中的描述性问题：哪些微生物特征与疗效相关？可用于支持“微生物群是疗效关键决定因素”的观点，并提供具体菌属和多样性指标作为证据。

facet_contributions.boundaries: 许多机制细节主要来自基础或转化研究，文中指出这些机制在临床人群中的验证仍不充分；不同代谢物的浓度依赖性效应复杂（如butyrate的双刃剑效应）；机制链条在人体内的完整性和特异性尚未完全确立。
facet_contributions.contribution: 综述了已知的微生物-免疫机制通路，包括：inosine轴（Bifidobacterium pseudolongum -> A2A受体 -> CD8+ T细胞）、SCFAs（acetate/propionate -> DCs; butyrate -> Treg/memory T cells）、次级胆汁酸（Clostridium scindens -> TGR5 -> Th1 bias）和色氨酸代谢物（Fusobacterium nucleatum -> AhR -> 抑制T细胞趋化）。
facet_contributions.possible_uses: 直接用于回答“介导效应的机制是什么”。提供具体的分子和细胞机制示例，解释微生物如何通过代谢物影响抗原呈递、T细胞浸润和功能。

facet_contributions.boundaries: 干预性研究多为早期阶段、单中心、小样本，证据等级中等；FMT的供体依赖性是一个重大挑战；饮食干预的自我报告偏差；Vidutolimod研究未根据微生物组成进行前瞻性分层，因果关系不明。
facet_contributions.contribution: 评估了多种微生物靶向干预策略的临床效果，包括FMT（ORR 20-40%）、高纤维饮食（改善PFS/OS）、Vidutolimod+Nivolumab（MPR ~55%），并对比了抗生素和益生菌的负面影响。引入了跨干预措施的元效应评分概念。
facet_contributions.possible_uses: 用于回答“哪些微生物干预策略有效”的问题。提供不同干预手段的效果大小、适用人群（如难治性黑色素瘤）和潜在风险（如抗生素损害疗效）。可用于指导未来干预策略的选择和优先级排序。

facet_contributions.boundaries: 模型多在特定癌种（如直肠癌）中开发和小规模验证；需要大规模前瞻性验证才能临床常规应用；不同研究间的测序方法和算法差异限制了通用性。
facet_contributions.contribution: 介绍了基于微生物组的预测模型（如SPEED模型，AUC>0.75；ML分类器AUC 0.83-0.92）及其在患者分层和疗效预测中的潜力。
facet_contributions.possible_uses: 用于讨论“如何利用微生物信息进行精准医疗”。提供预测模型的具体性能指标和应用场景（如直肠癌pCR预测），展示微生物组从生物标志物向临床决策工具的转变。

review_planning_B.planning_summary: 该综述为理解肠道微生物群如何作为ICI疗效的关键决定因素提供了全面的临床视角。它不仅汇总了微生物特征（多样性、特定菌属）与预后的关联，还详细评估了多种干预手段（FMT、饮食、抗生素、益生菌、药物组合）的临床效果，并引入了跨干预措施的定性比较框架。对于综述而言，它是梳理“微生物-免疫-疗效”关系、识别关键干预靶点（如避免抗生素、利用FMT/饮食）以及理解当前方法学局限性的核心素材。
scope_interpretation_cautions: 该综述主要为叙事性综合，非系统性荟萃分析，结果不应被解读为经过严格统计合并的效应量估计。
大部分证据来自观察性研究或小规模早期临床试验，因果推断需谨慎，特别是关于抗生素和益生菌的负面效应，可能存在混杂因素。
黑色素瘤数据最为丰富，对其他实体瘤的结论外推时需考虑肿瘤特异性和微环境差异。
机制部分引用的分子通路多基于基础或转化研究，其在广泛临床人群中的普遍性和重要性仍需更多临床验证。
预测模型的AUC值来自不同研究，直接比较其性能需谨慎，因训练集、验证集和特征工程可能存在差异。
topic_handles: 短链脂肪酸 (SCFAs) 及其代谢产物
粪便微生物移植 (FMT) - 供体来源与疗效
抗生素暴露 (时间窗与类别)
益生菌 (非靶向 vs. 靶向)
微生物组预测模型 (SPEED, ML classifiers)
跨干预措施元效应评分 (Meta-effect score)

study_summary_A.approach: 采用叙事性综述方法。检索PubMed/MEDLINE、Embase和Cochrane Library数据库（2015-2025年），筛选出评估肠道微生物群与癌症免疫治疗关系的95项人类临床研究。由两名审稿人独立提取数据并进行偏倚风险评估（使用Cochrane RoB 2、ROBINS-I等工具）。由于研究设计和结局的高度异质性，未进行正式荟萃分析，而是采用结构化叙述综合，强调机制合理性、转化相关性和跨癌症类型/干预模式的一致性。此外，还进行了跨干预措施的元效应评分分析以定性比较不同干预措施的临床价值。

contribution_and_limits.contribution: 提供了截至2025年关于肠道微生物群影响ICI疗效的全面临床证据综述，特别强调了抗生素和益生菌的负面作用以及FMT和高纤维饮食的潜在益处。
contribution_and_limits.limits: 所给摘要未交代具体的文献检索式细节（除关键词外）；由于研究异质性大，无法进行定量荟萃分析；证据等级多为中等或低等，缺乏高确定性证据；黑色素瘤研究占主导，其他肿瘤类型的泛化性受限；观察性研究多，因果推断能力有限。

key_findings.conditions: 接受ICI治疗的实体瘤患者（特别是黑色素瘤和NSCLC）
key_findings.finding: 较高的基线肠道微生物多样性（尤其是Faith's系统发育多样性）与更好的无进展生存期（PFS）和总生存期（OS）相关；富集共生菌（如Akkermansia muciniphila, Ruminococcaceae, Faecalibacterium）及短链脂肪酸（SCFA）产生菌有助于改善疗效。

key_findings.conditions: ICI治疗期间或启动前30天内使用广谱抗生素
key_findings.finding: consistently与较差的临床结局相关，包括PFS和OS显著降低（死亡风险比HR 1.4-2.0），且这种负面影响跨越多种肿瘤类型，提示为类效应。

key_findings.conditions: 使用非靶向的商业混合益生菌
key_findings.finding: consistently与较差的ICI疗效相关（ORR降低，PFS缩短），可能原因是降低了微生物多样性并导致特定菌属过度代表。

key_findings.conditions: 来自ICI响应者的粪便微生物移植（FMT）
key_findings.finding: 在难治性黑色素瘤的早期I/II期临床试验中，客观缓解率（ORR）达到20-40%，部分患者出现持久反应；机制涉及供体微生物群的定植和抗肿瘤免疫激活（CD8+ T细胞浸润增加）。

key_findings.conditions: 高纤维饮食或植物导向型饮食干预
key_findings.finding: 与改善的PFS和OS相关，机制上促进SCFA产生菌（如Ruminococcaceae）的富集，增加粪便丁酸和乙酸水平，并与更高的肿瘤内T细胞浸润相关。

key_findings.conditions: 基于微生物组的预测模型（如SPEED模型）
key_findings.finding: 在直肠癌新辅助治疗中，SPEED模型预测病理完全缓解（pCR）的AUC超过0.75；整合16S或宏基因组特征的机器学习分类器预测ICI反应的AUC为0.83-0.92。

study_summary_A.problem_or_question: 尽管免疫检查点抑制剂（ICIs）改变了肿瘤学治疗格局，但其疗效在不同患者间差异巨大（仅20-40%获得持久获益）。除了PD-L1表达、TMB和MSI等传统生物标志物外，寻找能更准确预测疗效的新生物标志物并探索通过调节肠道微生物群来增强疗效的临床策略是当前的主要问题。
study_summary_A.research_scope: 人类临床研究中肠道微生物群与癌症免疫治疗（特别是免疫检查点抑制剂，ICI）疗效之间的关系。涵盖实体瘤（黑色素瘤、非小细胞肺癌、肾细胞癌等），时间跨度为2015年至2025年3月。
study_summary_A.work_summary: 这是一篇叙事性综述，旨在综合过去十年中关于肠道微生物群在调节癌症免疫治疗反应中的作用的临床证据。研究评估了微生物群作为预测生物标志物和靶向治疗靶点的功能，重点介绍了机制见解、临床干预措施和转化意义。通过对95项临床研究（包括随机试验、前瞻性队列、回顾性分析和早期阶段干预研究）的叙述性综合，论文总结了微生物多样性、特定菌属、饮食、抗生素使用、益生菌、粪便微生物移植（FMT）以及机器学习模型对ICI疗效的影响。

auxiliary_material: The review synthesized 95 clinical studies (2015–2025) but precluded formal meta-analysis due to methodological heterogeneity in sampling (stool versus mucosal biopsy) and sequencing.
A cross-intervention meta-effect score analysis rated FMT and dietary fiber as positive (+1.0) and antibiotics/probiotics as negative (−1.0), providing a qualitative framework for intervention value.
The authors explicitly state that variability in sample collection and lack of standardization hinder the comparison of metabolite data across studies.

Predictive models like SPEED (AUC > 0.75) and machine-learning classifiers (AUC 0.83–0.92) are mentioned as tools integrating microbiome profiles, though these focus on taxonomy or composite scores rather than absolute metabolite concentrations.

useful_material: This study identifies specific microbial metabolites mechanistically linked to ICI response, including inosine (via Bifidobacterium pseudolongum and A2A receptor on CD8+ T cells) and short-chain fatty acids (acetate, propionate, butyrate affecting dendritic cells and T-cell memory).

The authors report that metabolomic profiling in dietary fiber studies demonstrated higher fecal butyrate and acetate levels correlating with greater intratumoral T-cell infiltration, though absolute tumor tissue concentrations were not specified in this text.

This review notes that three metabolomic studies integrated microbiome and metabolite data to predict treatment outcomes (specifically adverse events with AUC 0.963 using fecal and plasma profiles), indicating the existence of quantitative metabolite datasets in the field.

The discussion highlights the complexity of metabolite stoichiometry and immune contexture, noting that high concentrations of butyrate can suppress IL-2-dependent memory formation while acetate/propionate enhance dendritic cell fitness.

Predictive models like SPEED (AUC > 0.75) and machine-learning classifiers (AUC 0.83–0.92) are mentioned as tools integrating microbiome profiles, though these focus on taxonomy or composite scores rather than absolute metabolite concentrations.

useful_material: This study identifies specific microbial metabolites mechanistically linked to ICI response, including inosine (via Bifidobacterium pseudolongum and A2A receptor on CD8+ T cells) and short-chain fatty acids (acetate, propionate, butyrate affecting dendritic cells and T-cell memory).

The authors report that metabolomic profiling in dietary fiber studies demonstrated higher fecal butyrate and acetate levels correlating with greater intratumoral T-cell infiltration, though absolute tumor tissue concentrations were not specified in this text.

This review notes that three metabolomic studies integrated microbiome and metabolite data to predict treatment outcomes (specifically adverse events with AUC 0.963 using fecal and plasma profiles), indicating the existence of quantitative metabolite datasets in the field.

The discussion highlights the complexity of metabolite stoichiometry and immune contexture, noting that high concentrations of butyrate can suppress IL-2-dependent memory formation while acetate/propionate enhance dendritic cell fitness.

source_materials.title: Clinical Evidence for Microbiome-Based Strategies in Cancer Immunotherapy: A State-of-the-Art Review

broader_review_uses.connection_to_review: Helps establish the scientific basis for investigating GM-ICI interactions in solid tumors.
broader_review_uses.material: Introduction sections discussing the role of GMs in health and disease, and the rationale for combining GM modulation with ICIs and antiangiogenic therapy.
broader_review_uses.purpose: Contextual background on the importance of GMs in cancer therapy

broader_review_uses.connection_to_review: Provides concrete examples of how GM modulation has been tested in clinical settings, including dosing, patient populations, and observed effects.
broader_review_uses.material: Tables 1, 2, and 3 listing various clinical trials involving ICIs, antiangiogenic agents, and GM-modulating interventions.
broader_review_uses.purpose: Examples of clinical trial designs and outcomes

broader_review_uses.connection_to_review: Offers critical perspectives on the feasibility and risks of GM-based therapies, which can be contrasted with other reviews focusing solely on efficacy.
broader_review_uses.material: Sections on safety concerns (e.g., FMT-related infections), lack of specificity in probiotics, and individual variability.
broader_review_uses.purpose: Discussion of challenges and limitations

facet_contributions.boundaries: Most evidence is correlative or from small-scale trials. Causality is often inferred from animal models. The paper notes variability in results across different cancer types.
facet_contributions.contribution: Provides a summary of clinical trials and observational studies showing associations between specific GM compositions (e.g., high abundance of Bifidobacterium, Akkermansia) and improved response to ICIs in solid tumors. Lists specific bacterial taxa and metabolites linked to better outcomes.
facet_contributions.possible_uses: Can be used to support arguments about the predictive value of baseline gut microbiome composition for ICI efficacy. Provides examples of successful combinations (e.g., FMT + Pembrolizumab).

facet_contributions.boundaries: Many mechanisms are derived from mouse models and may not fully translate to human physiology. The paper acknowledges that exact mechanisms remain incompletely understood. Some claims are based on limited human data.
facet_contributions.contribution: Details several proposed mechanisms by which GMs modulate ICI efficacy, including DC maturation, T-cell activation, and regulation of immunosuppressive cells (Tregs, MDSCs). Also describes mechanisms related to angiogenesis, such as metabolite-induced VEGF regulation.
facet_contributions.possible_uses: Useful for explaining potential biological pathways linking GMs to immune response. Can illustrate how different interventions (probiotics, FMT, diet) might exert effects via distinct mechanisms.

review_planning_B.planning_summary: This paper serves as a broad contextual resource for understanding the intersection of gut microbiome modulation, angiogenesis, and immune checkpoint inhibition. It provides a structured framework for discussing how GMs influence the tumor microenvironment and host immunity. While it does not offer deep mechanistic details for every pathway, it lists numerous specific bacterial species, metabolites, and clinical trial examples that can be used to illustrate the diversity of GM-therapy interactions. It is particularly useful for establishing the rationale for combining GM modulation with standard cancer therapies and for highlighting the current limitations in clinical translation.
scope_interpretation_cautions: This is a perspective/review article; findings are synthesized from other studies and should not be treated as primary empirical evidence.
Many mechanisms described are based on preclinical models; direct applicability to human patients is not confirmed.
The paper highlights heterogeneity in GM composition and response across individuals and cancer types, cautioning against over-generalization.
Claims about specific bacterial strains or metabolites are often based on limited or preliminary data.
topic_handles: Metabolites: Inosine, Short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs), LPS

study_summary_A.approach: As a perspective/review article, this work does not present new primary experimental data. Instead, it synthesizes existing literature from preclinical studies (mouse models) and clinical trials. The authors organize the content by first describing the composition and function of the gut microbiome, then detailing its impact on tumor angiogenesis and immune responses. They subsequently review various modulation strategies (probiotics, FMT, diet, engineering) and summarize relevant clinical trial data presented in tables. Finally, they discuss the translational challenges and future directions.

contribution_and_limits.contribution: Provides a comprehensive overview of the dual role of GMs in regulating both angiogenesis and immune checkpoint inhibition in cancer.
contribution_and_limits.limits: As a perspective piece, it relies on summarizing existing literature rather than generating new causal evidence. Many mechanisms described are based on preclinical models, and direct translation to humans remains uncertain.

contribution_and_limits.contribution: Summarizes a wide range of clinical trials and preclinical studies linking GM composition to ICI and antiangiogenic therapy outcomes.
contribution_and_limits.limits: The review does not provide a systematic meta-analysis or quantitative synthesis of the clinical data. Specificity of beneficial bacterial strains varies across studies, making generalization difficult.

contribution_and_limits.contribution: Identifies key challenges such as safety risks of FMT and lack of specificity in probiotic interventions.
contribution_and_limits.limits: Does not offer definitive solutions to these challenges but highlights them as areas for future research.

key_findings.conditions: Preclinical models and observational clinical data
key_findings.finding: Specific GMs (e.g., Bifidobacterium, Akkermansia muciniphila) and their metabolites (e.g., inosine, short-chain fatty acids) are associated with enhanced efficacy of ICIs by promoting dendritic cell maturation, T-cell activation, and reducing immunosuppressive cells.

key_findings.conditions: Mechanistic studies in vitro and in vivo
key_findings.finding: GMs can regulate angiogenesis through metabolites like LPS, lipoteichoic acid, and butyrate, which affect VEGF expression and endothelial cell function. Some bacteria promote angiogenesis, while others inhibit it.

key_findings.conditions: Clinical observations
key_findings.finding: Antibiotic use is consistently associated with worse survival and reduced efficacy in patients receiving ICIs, suggesting GMs play a critical role in treatment response.

key_findings.conditions: Intervention studies
key_findings.finding: FMT from responders to ICIs can restore efficacy in non-responders in some cases. Engineered bacteria (e.g., SYNB1891) show promise in activating innate immunity in combination with ICIs.

study_summary_A.problem_or_question: The paper addresses the problem that many patients do not respond to or develop resistance to ICIs and antiangiogenic therapies. It seeks to understand how the gut microbiome influences these treatments and explores potential methods to leverage GMs to improve therapeutic outcomes.
study_summary_A.research_scope: The paper focuses on the interaction between gut microbes (GMs) and cancer therapy, specifically examining their role in modulating immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) and antiangiogenic agents. It covers human physiology, tumor microenvironment (TME), preclinical models, and clinical trials involving various solid tumors.
study_summary_A.work_summary: This perspective article reviews the complex relationship between the gut microbiome and cancer treatment efficacy. It discusses how GMs influence both angiogenesis in the tumor microenvironment and the response to immune checkpoint blockade. The authors summarize current strategies for manipulating GMs—including probiotics, fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT), dietary interventions, and engineered bacteria—to enhance the effectiveness of combined ICI and antiangiogenic therapies. The paper also highlights the challenges and opportunities for translating these findings into clinical practice, noting safety concerns and the need for more specific mechanistic understanding.

tool_materials.question: What are the measured physiological concentrations of inosine and SCFAs inside the human tumour microenvironment correlating with ICI response?
tool_materials.still_missing: The supplied material does not provide data on inosine concentrations, which is a specific requirement of the gap question. Furthermore, while the success criteria allow for serum data, the gap question prioritizes concentrations 'inside the human tumour microenvironment'; this study measured peripheral plasma and fecal concentrations, not intratumoral tissue concentrations. Therefore, the physiological levels of SCFAs and inosine specifically within the tumour tissue remain unaddressed. The success criterion for quantitative data of specific metabolites is partially met for SCFAs in plasma but unmet for inosine and tumour tissue.
tool_materials.usable_content: This prospective cohort study (n=52) measured quantitative concentrations of short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) in human plasma and fecal samples from patients with solid tumors treated with PD-1 inhibitors. The authors reported median concentrations in μmol/g for multiple SCFAs, linking them to immune checkpoint inhibitor outcomes. Specifically, fecal propionic acid concentrations were significantly higher in responders (median 172.6 μmol/g) compared to nonresponders (median 103.6 μmol/g), and high fecal propionic acid was independently associated with longer progression-free survival (multivariate HR, 0.07; 95% CI, 0.03-0.19). Plasma isovaleric acid was also significantly higher in responders (median 0.3 μmol/g) vs nonresponders (median 0.0 μmol/g) and associated with progression-free survival (HR, 0.38; 95% CI, 0.14-0.99). Other measured SCFAs included acetic, butyric, valeric, isobutyric, hydroangelic, caproic, and succinic acids in both matrices. This provides quantitative metabolite data in a systemic biofluid (plasma) correlated with ICI efficacy, addressing the 'serum' and 'quantitative data' aspects of the success criteria for SCFAs. ['This study identifies inosine and short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) as microbiota-derived metabolites with biological relevance to T-cell differentiation and immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) efficacy, citing proof-of-principle evidence for inosine in mice (Section 5.1).', 'The authors explicitly state that paired measurements of candidate metabolites, including SCFAs and amino-acid pools, in stool, portal or peripheral blood, tumor tissue, and tumor interstitial fluid are currently lacking in the literature (Section 5.1).', 'Table 1 provides quantitative data on fecal SCFAs from human intervention studies (e.g., Ahmad et al. 2020; Kwok et al. 2024), though these were conducted in healthy adults without ICI therapy and measured stool rather than tumor concentrations.', 'Section 3 details challenges in exposure assessment and metabolite measurement, noting that urinary biomarkers exist for some compounds but direct tumor microenvironment quantification remains a methodological gap.', 'The review distinguishes between contextual microbiome-ICI evidence (where inosine/SCFAs are mentioned as affecting T-cell fitness) and direct NNS-ICI evidence, clarifying that metabolite-ICI links often derive from studies not testing the specific exposure of interest (Section 6.1).'] This narrative review establishes a mechanistic framework (Microbiome → Metabolites → Immune Modulation → TME State → ICI Response) linking gut microbial metabolites to immune checkpoint inhibitor efficacy. The authors detail short-chain fatty acid (SCFA) mechanisms, including G-protein-coupled receptor binding and histone deacetylase inhibition, and explain that SCFA immune outcomes are concentration-dependent and microenvironment-specific (e.g., physiological mucosal concentrations favor Treg induction, while tumor-inflamed environments may favor CD8+ T-cell enhancement). Crucially, the authors explicitly state that the concentration-response relationship for SCFAs in human tumor-bearing contexts has not been characterized. The text does not contain any mention of inosine.

tool_materials.question: Are there any recent human studies (2024-2026) that validate strain-specific immune mechanisms (e.g., DC maturation by a specific bacterium) in solid tumor patients beyond correlation?
tool_materials.still_missing: While the study links the specific strain to immune changes in patients, the human data primarily demonstrates pharmacodynamic associations (pre-post treatment changes or responder vs. non-responder comparisons) rather than causal validation of the specific immune mechanism (e.g., proving TLR4-mediated DC maturation) within the human patients themselves. The deep mechanistic pathway (TLR4, M2-M1 repolarization) is validated in preclinical models, leaving the human mechanistic validation at the level of immune marker modulation consistent with the hypothesis but not experimentally proven beyond correlation in the clinical cohort.
tool_materials.usable_content: This study is a prospective, first-in-human Phase I trial (NCT05877430, 2023-2025) evaluating a specific bacterial strain, CJRB-101 (Leuconostoc mesenteroides), combined with pembrolizumab in solid tumor patients (NSCLC, HNSCC, melanoma). It meets the temporal and population criteria. The authors confirmed strain-specific engraftment via stool metagenomics (increased L. mesenteroides abundance) and measured immune mechanisms in patients, including upregulation of immune activation genes (CCL5, TLR9, CD3E) in on-treatment samples, reduction of PD-1+TIM-3+ T cells and PMN-MDSCs in peripheral blood, and spatial profiling showing increased GZB+CD8+ T cells in tumor tissue. These data link the specific strain administration to measured immune pharmacodynamic effects in ICI-treated patients. tool_materials.usable_content: ['This study experimentally validates the function of ICI-associated bacterial strains (Enterococcus genus) using gnotobiotic and antibiotic-pretreated mouse tumor models (B16-F10 melanoma, MC38, MCA205).', 'Specific human-commensal strains (e.g., E. faecium Com15) were orally administered to mice and shown to significantly enhance anti-PD-L1, anti-PD-1, and anti-CTLA-4 efficacy compared to non-protective strains (e.g., E. faecalis OG1RF).', 'The study distinguishes genomic potential from functional validation by identifying the SagA peptidoglycan hydrolase gene, confirming its enzymatic activity in vitro, and proving sufficiency via heterologous expression in E. faecalis and Lactococcus lactis.', 'Functional validation included metabolite measurement/administration: synthetic Nod2-active muropeptides (MDP-L,D) replicated the antitumor effect, confirming the molecular mechanism beyond live bacterial colonization.', "Mechanistic validation established host dependency: the antitumor effect was abrogated in Nod2-/- mice, confirming the specific host receptor pathway required for the strain's function."] This study experimentally validates the functional capacity of responder versus non-responder gut microbiota communities using fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) into gnotobiotic mice, demonstrating that responder microbiota decreases tumor growth following ICI treatment. It identifies specific Amplicon Sequence Variants (ASVs) belonging to genera such as Colidextribacter, Frisingicoccus, Marvinbryantia, and Blautia that overlap between human responders and colonized mice, correlating with tumor size. Crucially for the gap, the authors explicitly state in the Conclusions and Discussion that 'The role of isolate-specific function... has been underappreciated' and that the work 'supports further investigation using isolate-driven models,' indicating that isolation and validation of specific strains from these ASVs had not been performed in this study and remains a necessary future step. The review explicitly distinguishes between human observational associations and preclinical experimental validation. It documents that while fecal transplantation from human responders to mice recapitulates outcomes (e.g., references [19–21]), these studies often 'did not further identify the specific bacteria whose abundance was associated with immune responses' and highlights the need for 'inoculation with single-lineage bacteria.' It lists specific genera validated in preclinical models via oral gavage (e.g., Bifidobacterium spp., Bacteroides fragilis, Akkermansia muciniphila, Enterococcus hirae) but notes inconsistencies when compared to human cohort data (e.g., Bacteroidales associated with response in some studies, non-response in others). The text explicitly states that 'improvements in the isolation of cultivable bacteria and derivation of individual clones... may represent future steps,' indicating that comprehensive strain-level experimental validation linked to human cohorts is currently lacking or incomplete.

updated_plan.reader_objective: 使读者清晰理解微生物群调制 ICI 疗效的三大核心生物学路径，掌握关键菌种/代谢物的作用靶点与浓度阈值，并能准确评估临床前因果证据与人类观察性数据的证据等级差异，从而在撰写综述时合理界定机制假设与确证事实的边界。
updated_plan.thesis: 肠道微生物群通过免疫启动（DC/T 细胞互作）、代谢物信号（SCFAs、肌苷、色氨酸/胆汁酸受体通路）及屏障完整性/细菌易位三大路径调制实体瘤 ICI 疗效；临床前模型确立了明确的因果链条，但人类数据多为观察性关联，需严格区分物种差异与肿瘤类型特异性，避免将动物模型结论直接外推为临床事实。肌苷等关键代谢物的人类肿瘤微环境浓度数据尚缺，现有证据主要依赖血浆相关性与小鼠模型。

case_suggestions.proposed_use: 提供 Ruminococcaceae 通过 TLRs 刺激 CD103+ DCs 经 IRF8/NFATc1 通路增强 CD8+ T 细胞激活的具体分子例证，支撑"细菌-DC-T 细胞轴"的因果链条与临床前验证逻辑。
引入异源记忆 T 细胞与分子模拟假说，解释预存微生物暴露史如何通过 TCR 交叉反应性重塑新抗原免疫原性，补充传统 DC 介导路径之外的宿主背景维度。
提供 SFB 诱导肠道 TH17 细胞迁移至肿瘤并发生表型可塑性转化为促炎 TH1 样细胞的实证，支撑"分子模拟假说"下抗原交叉反应与 T 细胞远程招募的因果链条。
补充 MAMPs/PRRs（TLR/NOD 通路）激活 DC 成熟及分子模拟假说的具体分子路径，支撑"细菌-DC-T 细胞轴"的因果链条与临床前验证逻辑。

paragraph_briefs.development: 比较双歧杆菌、阿克曼氏菌与肠球菌对 DC 表型（MHC-I/II、CD80/86、IL-12 分泌）的调控差异；引入 SagA 肽聚糖水解酶/NOD2 轴作为分子开关，说明特定菌株如何突破稳态触发 DC 活化。
paragraph_briefs.point: DC 成熟是免疫启动的限速步骤，不同共生菌通过 PRRs/NOD2 轴差异化调控 DC 表型。

paragraph_briefs.development: 阐述微生物抗原与肿瘤新抗原序列同源性如何诱导预存记忆 T 细胞克隆；结合肌苷通过 UBA6 抑制解除 MHC-I 类分子加工限制的非经典途径，说明微生物如何通过双重靶向增强内在免疫原性。
paragraph_briefs.point: 分子模拟假说提供交叉反应性 T 细胞扩增的机制桥梁，补充传统 DC-T 细胞轴之外的非经典路径。

paragraph_briefs.development: 对比无菌鼠/人源化鼠定植实验的强因果效力与人类队列的观察性局限；强调物种间 DC 发育轨迹与 TLR 信号通路的差异，警示跨物种外推的局限性。
paragraph_briefs.point: 临床前因果证据与人类观察性数据的证据等级差异警示直接外推风险。

units.synthesis: 免疫启动路径揭示了共生菌如何通过 PRR/NOD2 轴与分子模拟桥接先天与适应性免疫，构成 ICI 疗效增强的第一道防线。然而，该路径的效能高度依赖宿主 DC 发育轨迹与 TLR 信号基线，临床前强因果链在人类中多表现为观察性关联。
units.transition: 除细胞互作外，可溶性小分子同样构成关键的远程调制网络，其效能取决于受体亲和力与微环境浓度阈值。
units.unit_title: 免疫启动路径：树突状细胞成熟与 T 细胞交叉反应/致敏

case_suggestions.proposed_use: 系统梳理 IPA、丁酸、肌苷等代谢物通过 HDAC 抑制、AHR 激活及 A2AR 信号重编程 T 细胞的剂量依赖性与组织特异性机制，支撑 SCFAs 双刃剑效应与情境阈值论述。
详述肌苷作为嘌呤代谢中间产物，既可通过腺苷 A2A 受体（A2AR）促进 Th1 分化，又直接进入肿瘤细胞抑制泛素激活酶 UBA6，解除对 MHC-I 类分子加工的限制，从而增强内在免疫原性。明确标注人类 TME 浓度数据缺失。
详述微生物次级胆汁酸（如 3-oxo-LCA）通过 RORγt 调节 Th17/Treg 平衡的分子细节，补充胆汁酸轴双向免疫调节案例。
提供 TMAO、胆汁酸与 SCFAs 在不同癌种中双向调节的实证对比，阐释代谢物效应的浓度依赖性与受体特异性，支撑双刃剑效应论述。

paragraph_briefs.development: 详述丁酸/丙酸在生理黏膜浓度下促进 Treg 分化，而在肿瘤炎症微环境中通过 HDAC 抑制上调 MHC-I 并增强 CD8+ T 细胞杀伤力；引用定量浓度数据说明阈值效应与微环境 pH/氧分压的情境依赖性。强调人类 TME 内 SCFA 直接浓度数据缺失，现有证据基于粪便/血浆样本。
paragraph_briefs.point: SCFAs 的浓度依赖性与情境依赖性呈现双刃剑效应。

paragraph_briefs.development: 阐述肌苷作为嘌呤代谢中间产物，既可通过腺苷 A2A 受体（A2AR）促进 Th1 分化，又直接进入肿瘤细胞抑制泛素激活酶 UBA6，解除对 MHC-I 类分子加工的限制，从而增强内在免疫原性。明确指出人类肿瘤微环境内肌苷绝对浓度数据尚未测定，现有证据依赖 CheckMate 025 血浆相关性（中位 OS 33 个月 vs. 22 个月）与小鼠模型验证。
paragraph_briefs.point: 肌苷通过 A2AR 与 UBA6 的双向靶向克服 ICI 耐药，但人类 TME 浓度数据缺失。

paragraph_briefs.development: 对比促炎/抗炎分支：犬尿氨酸激活 AhR 促进 Treg/MDSC 积累导致耐药；而吲哚衍生物（IPA/IAA）激活 AhR 或核受体（FXR/TGR5）可逆转免疫抑制；胆汁酸（UDCA vs DCA/LCA）呈现剂量与受体依赖的双刃剑效应。
paragraph_briefs.point: 色氨酸-AhR 轴与胆汁酸核受体的双向免疫调节。

units.synthesis: 代谢物信号揭示了远程调制的生化基础，其效能高度依赖受体表达谱、浓度阈值与微环境理化参数。这些可溶性信号构成了连接肠道生态与远端 TME 的分子桥梁，但其双向效应要求精准干预而非盲目补充。人类肿瘤微环境内代谢物绝对浓度数据缺失，现有证据主要依赖外周样本相关性与临床前模型。
units.transition: 代谢物信号的"泄漏"程度与局部微环境重塑，根本上受制于肠道物理屏障的完整性；屏障破坏引发的细菌易位成为第三条关键调制路径。
units.unit_title: 代谢物信号通路：受体介导的表观遗传与转录重编程

case_suggestions.proposed_use: 利用肠-on-a-chip 模型实证非响应者菌群导致 ZO-1/E-cadherin 下调与屏障通透性增加，而鞭毛蛋白可恢复稳态，为易位时空动态与屏障修复策略提供体外对照。
揭示 ICT 诱导肠道细菌经 DC 摄取迁移至肠系膜淋巴结的物理转移路径，填补"微生物存在"与"远端免疫"间的因果链条。
通过 FMT 小鼠实验展示产丁酸菌缺失与肠球菌富集直接诱导结肠炎，阐明屏障破坏后微生物信号泄漏触发局部过度炎症的病理表型与毒性权衡。
批判性评估肠道屏障修复剂与有益信号"泄漏"之间的平衡难题，提供空间隔室差异视角，支撑易位调控策略的临床转化潜力讨论。

paragraph_briefs.development: 分析紧密连接蛋白（ZO-1, Occludin）与杯状细胞黏液层在维持生态位中的作用；对比健康稳态与菌群失调（如抗生素暴露、高脂饮食）下的通透性变化及其对循环内毒素水平的直接影响。
paragraph_briefs.point: 屏障完整性决定微生物信号的系统性"泄漏"阈值。

paragraph_briefs.development: 阐述易位细菌如何被引流淋巴结捕获并触发远端抗肿瘤免疫景观重塑；结合空间多组学与活体成像证据说明易位的时空动态，并指出同一易位事件可能同时驱动抗肿瘤效应与 irAEs 发生。
paragraph_briefs.point: 易位细菌被次级淋巴器官捕获后触发远端抗肿瘤免疫或引发 irAEs。

paragraph_briefs.development: 探讨屏障修复剂、靶向益生菌清除易位病原体及空间控释递送系统的转化前景；强调需在恢复屏障稳态与保留有益信号"泄漏"之间取得平衡。
paragraph_briefs.point: 屏障修复策略与易位调控的临床转化潜力。

units.synthesis: 屏障完整性是决定微生物信号系统性"泄漏"的物理闸门；易位事件既可重塑远端抗肿瘤免疫景观，也可能诱发 irAEs，凸显了物理屏障在调制治疗窗口中的核心地位。
units.transition: 三大路径共同构成微生物调制 ICI 疗效的网络，但临床前因果链与人类观察性数据之间存在显著证据鸿沟，需明确界定转化边界。
units.unit_title: 屏障功能与细菌易位：物理屏障破坏与局部/系统性免疫重塑

case_suggestions.proposed_use: 提出跨癌种生态分层视角（安娜·卡列尼娜原则），论证从单一菌种寻找转向生态系统稳定性与功能代谢谱预测的范式转变，解释队列间结果异质性的生态学根源。
以 MIMic 一期试验报告了 FMT+ 抗 PD1 在晚期黑色素瘤中的临床结果（ORR 65%、mPFS 29.6 月、mOS 52.8 月），并发现响应者富集 SCFA 产生菌，为临床前因果证据与人类观察性数据的证据等级差异提供直接对照。
展示 FMT-LUMINate II 期试验在 NSCLC（ORR 80%）和黑色素瘤（ORR 75%）中的临床活性，强调响应与基线有害菌清除而非供体定植相关，为转化边界讨论提供实证。
提供跨干预措施元效应评分框架，将 FMT、高纤维饮食评为正向（+1.0），抗生素、益生菌评为负向（-1.0），为转化准备度评估提供定性比较基准。

paragraph_briefs.development: 对比无菌鼠/人源化鼠定植实验的强因果效力与人类队列（如 P0613, P0490）的观察性局限；强调物种间 DC 发育轨迹、TLR 信号基线与肿瘤微环境理化参数的差异，警示直接外推风险。
paragraph_briefs.point: 临床前因果链的强效力与人类观察性数据的异质性形成证据鸿沟。

paragraph_briefs.development: 分析黑色素瘤、NSCLC、RCC、CRC 等癌种间菌群基线、ICI 响应阈值与代谢物阈值的显著差异；指出 16S rRNA 与宏基因组测序、样本采集与存储流程的不一致如何放大结果异质性。
paragraph_briefs.point: 肿瘤类型特异性与测序方法学差异加剧结果不可比性。

paragraph_briefs.development: 总结当前证据等级（临床前强因果 vs 人类中等/低确定性观察），提出 III 期 RCT、多中心标准化采样、配对血清/肿瘤组织代谢物定量及 AI 辅助多组学整合的优先事项；明确当前仅支持谨慎的抗生素管理与探索性 FMT，不支持常规益生菌推荐。
paragraph_briefs.point: 转化准备度评估：从概念验证到标准化 RCT 的必经之路。

units.synthesis: 三大调制路径共同构成微生物影响 ICI 疗效的网络，但临床前强因果链与人类观察性数据之间存在显著证据鸿沟。严格区分物种差异、肿瘤类型特异性与方法学异质性，是合理界定机制假设与确证事实边界的必要前提。人类 TME 代谢物定量数据缺失限制机制外推，个体异质性（饮食、药物）干扰机制解析。
units.transition: 本章机制解析为后续章节评估干预策略可行性、安全性与临床转化路线图奠定了生物学与证据等级基础。
units.unit_title: 证据等级整合与转化边界：临床前因果链与人类观察性数据的界限
